dropped.finding: The newly-added `check --ac --clarity` mutual-exclusivity contract (both flags together → exit 2) has no test. check_cli adds `if len(set(modes)) > 1: ... return 2` and the parser adds an argparse mutually-exclusive group, and docs/exit-codes.md documents '`--ac`/`--clarity` together → 2', but no test invokes `check <id> --ac --clarity`.
dropped.suggested_fix: In tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli_argparse.py, add a case asserting `main(["check", tid, "--ac", "--clarity"]) == 2` and that the stderr names the conflict.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the inspect.getsource grep in test_cli_read_arms_do_not_gate_on_bare_isdir with a behavioral assertion (or delete it, since the four parametrized tests already cover store-usability).
evidence: tests/unit/test_reads_cli_uninitialized_store.py:158: source = inspect.getsource(reads_cli._cmd_list)
tests/unit/test_reads_cli_uninitialized_store.py:159: assert "os.path.isdir(tracker)" not in source

The behavioral contract is already covered by test_cli_read_rejects_present_but_unusable_store_without_git / _midclone / _still_rejects_absent / _still_returns_empty_for_initialized_empty_store (lines 98-149), which assert exit code + stderr/stdout — the observable store-usability behavior.
dropped.finding: test_cli_read_arms_do_not_gate_on_bare_isdir asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of the unit under test (greps inspect.getsource(reads_cli._cmd_list) for the literal 'os.path.isdir(tracker)') rather than its behavior. It is a change-detector: it breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (extracting the usability check, or re-spelling it 'os.path.isdir(str(tracker))') and stays green if the usability behavior regresses but the literal string is simply absent. The four parametrized behavioral tests above it (broken/.git-less, mid-clone, absent, empty-but-valid) already pin the store-usability contract observably.
scenarios: A refactor that preserves store-usability behavior but renames/extracts the gate check turns this test red with no behavior change.
A regression that reintroduces a weak existence check spelled differently (e.g. Path(tracker).is_dir()) leaves this grep green.
